claims.citation: New York Herald, 15 May 1866, p. 5, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Brig Tiber, of Halifax, NS, Farrell, Shields, 90[?] days, with
merchandise, to H & F W Meyer. Had heavy weather,
carried away main yard and split sails. March 24, latitude
5[?] deg 20[?] min, longitude 6 deg 44[?] min, fell in with brig Har-
riet, of and from Ardrossan, for Bordeaux, coal laden, with
seven feet of water in the hold; ran close under her bow.
Three of the seamen of the Harriet jumped into our rigging;
lowered a boat and pulled around her, but saw no one on
board; supposed they were all drowned by the boat being
swamped, as she lay alongside filled; the brig sunk 11 A M
same day. March 26th, latitude 50[?] deg 49[?] min, longitude 6
deg 37[?] min, spoke pilot boat No 29[?], of Scilly, and put the three
seamen on board of her to be landed at Scilly.

claims.verbatim:
Brig Tiber (of Halifax, N. S.), Farrell, Shields 60 days, with mdse.
to H. & F. W. Meyer. Had heavy weather; carried away main yard
and split sails. March 24, in lat.[?] 51 20, long. 6 44, fell in with brig
Harriet (of and from Ardrossan for Bordeaux), coal laden, with 7 feet
of water in the hold; ran close under her bow; three of the seamen of
the H. jumped into our rigging; lowered a boat and pulled around her,
but saw no one on board; supposed they were drowned by the boat
being swamped; as she lay alongside, filled, and the brig sank at 11 a.
m., the same day. March 26, in lat 50[?] 49, long. 6 37, spoke pilot boat
No 20 of Scilly, and put the three seamen on board of her, to be
landed at Scilly.
